tasks.short: Retrieve and transfer checked medical data

steps.what: Retrieve medical records data for the identified patient and request
Capture missing data and confirm the source identity for inclusion in medical records
Enter the identified source data in the medical records staging fields
Check the staged medical data and physician recipient against the original request and source
Transmit the checked data packet to the requesting physicians for medical record review

tasks.design: Configure the patient-specific retrieval view in the clinical record system in {OTHER}, then use a validated field mapping for repeated transfer into its staging area. The transcriptionist checks source meaning, patient and recipient before the separate transfer to the physician's review queue.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing source data is retrieved and retyped across clinical screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views and supported field interfaces can reuse identified data without generating clinical facts.
tasks.still_hard: Patient identity, ambiguous source values and mismatched clinical context.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a source does not answer the physician's actual request.

ambition.what: No clinical decision authority is transferred.

reach.task: Reconcile staged data to source records
reach.learn: Patient identifiers and clinical field provenance.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: supported record-system interfaces can transfer structured fields, with source reconciliation and patient checks retained.

assumptions: Boundary is authorised retrieval, data entry and internal transfer to a physician review queue, not clinical sign-off or final publication. Physician review remains outside and unchanged.

Requesting physician supplies patient id, encounter id, requested fields and purpose. Existing source systems supply field value, units, time and source id; the transcriptionist captures missing values and verifies identity in s2. S3 consumes only this identified packet.

Test native retrieval and field reuse first. The 30-share s3 baseline is actual cross-screen re-entry, not a same-system save. Unsupported fields stop for manual repair in s4, with additional mapping failures funded by incremental upkeep.

Final staged packet exists before s4. Approval covers the exact patient, values and physician recipient transferred in s5; any change requires recheck. The one-share transfer has no claimed saving. No ordinary internal author save has a gate.
All shares are unmeasured focal labour estimates. The field contract and destination access must be confirmed locally; no new source-capture work is hidden.
unknowns: Supported source-to-staging interface and actual cross-screen retyping.
research_questions: Can the actual units and source timestamps survive transfer without interpretation?

already_counted.description: Source capture, identity checks, reconciliation and manual field exceptions remain.

incremental.description: Repair field mappings and manually handle failed transfers beyond routine checks.

approvals.approved_version: checked patient data and physician recipient snapshot from s4; changes invalidate it

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central lookup cut 16.25 plus re-entry removal 30 gives 46.25 gross and 44.75 net. Cautious case: no supported write interface leaves re-entry fully manual, while a native view leaves lookup at 55% retained; 11.25 gross less upkeep 1.5 gives 9.75, above low 8.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Turn clinical dictation into a checked transcript draft

steps.what: Identify the dictation encounter and check its recording context
Take dictation through the headset or recording console and manage unclear audio
Transcribe the dictation into the required clinical transcript draft

loop.purpose: Draft a faithful transcript from clinician dictation
loop.input: Identified audio segments and transcript template
loop.output: Transcript draft with audio-linked uncertain spans
loop.check: Transcriptionist compares every clinical statement, negation, number and name to the audio in s4
loop.stop: One draft; uncertain spans remain unresolved for manual transcription or clinician query
loop.why_not_simpler: Clinical speech and abbreviations cannot be converted by fixed field copying alone

steps.what: Check the dictation transcript against the audio and correct clinical terminology and omissions
Save the checked dictation transcript as an unsigned working draft

tasks.design: Test approved native dictation support in the clinical transcription system in {OTHER} before adding a bounded speech-to-text draft step. Keep audio capture, full clinical comparison and unresolved-span handling with the transcriptionist, then save an unsigned draft for the existing downstream clinician workflow.
tasks.previous_blocker: Typing clinical speech consumes attention alongside terminology checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Speech transcription can supply an editable draft with source-linked uncertainty.
tasks.still_hard: Negation, dose, identity and unclear speech errors can change clinical meaning.
tasks.human_edge: Notice a plausible sentence that does not match the recorded statement.

ambition.what: The transcriptionist gains no clinical signing authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: speech transcription can draft clinical dictation, but comparison to source audio and clinical author review remain necessary.

assumptions: Boundary is taking dictation through stored unsigned transcript. Sending for clinician sign-off is a downstream action, not silently automated; the stored draft is not a final dossier entry.

The clinician produces audio and encounter identifiers. The transcriptionist verifies the header in s1 and captures/manages audio in s2, so speech input is not free. Template and terminology lists are existing controlled resources.

Native approved dictation is tested first. S3 retains setup and manual typing of difficult spans; s4 retains full semantic proofreading and questions. Failed audio segments are transcribed manually there, with additional failure allowance in incremental work.
No open public model receives clinical material. Required local access, retention and workforce consultation are included in build ranges without claiming a particular legal outcome.
All shares are unmeasured focal labour estimates. The ordinary same-system working-draft save has no gate and no saving.
unknowns: Audio quality, permitted clinical transcription tooling and current speech recognition use.
research_questions: How much manual reconstruction remains on difficult dictations after full audio comparison?

already_counted.description: Audio handling, difficult-span transcription and full semantic comparison remain.

incremental.description: Check terminology configuration and manually recover failed recordings beyond routine draft corrections.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central draft typing cut 40 less upkeep 2 gives 38. Cautious case: noisy audio and specialised terminology leave s3 at 75% retained, yielding 12.5 gross and 10.5 net. Audio handling and full proofreading stay unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Handle clerical mail and claims with checked dispatch

steps.what: Sort incoming mail and clerical office items by patient, document type and destination
Prepare outgoing mail and operate the necessary office machines
Complete insurance claims using the existing encounter and billing fields
Check the final insurance claims and outgoing mail for source accuracy and intended recipient
Dispatch the checked outgoing mail packet
Submit the checked insurance claims to the payer
Complete clerical typing and filing of handled office items in the existing record index

tasks.design: Configure item routing, claim forms and record-index defaults in the clinical office system in {OTHER}. Keep physical mail preparation, final accuracy and recipient checks, and both dispatch actions with the transcriptionist; claim data is populated only from already authorised billing fields.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated sorting, claim-field copying and record indexing span office systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Native routing rules, field reuse and filing defaults remove specific clerical operations.
tasks.still_hard: Misaddressed clinical correspondence and unsupported claim information.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a document that belongs to another encounter or needs clinical clarification.

ambition.what: No new billing or clinical coding authority is proposed.

reach.task: Validate a claim against authorised encounter fields
reach.learn: Payer required fields and rejection reasons.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native claim forms, routing rules and record-index defaults can reuse structured billing and document identifiers without a model.

assumptions: This is an illustrative recurring office-work basket containing the listed mail, claims, typing and filing duties, not a measured universal mix. Actual mix must be established before a role roll-up. The filing in s7 is the existing clinical correspondence and claim record index, not an added activity log.

Existing intake staff or electronic message headers provide patient id, encounter id, document type and intended service; the transcriptionist checks or captures missing identifiers within retained s1 time. Clinicians and billing staff already authorise service date, code, payer and amount; s3 handles missing or changed fields manually in its retained time, not by inventing codes.

Test native rules and forms first. S1 removes only routine classification by existing identifiers; s3 removes repeated field entry; s7 removes repeated identifier typing and folder selection while preserving actual filing, unmatched items and tiny same-system saves.

Both final claim and mail packet exist before s4. Each release binds its own content and recipient snapshot; any edit voids that release. S5 and s6 retain all their already small action time. Ordinary internal filing needs no self-approval gate.
All shares are focal labour estimates. Other-role source authoring and payer processing remain unchanged outside labour. Incremental allowance funds rule maintenance and exceptional routing repair.
unknowns: Actual local basket mix, existing routing and payer-field completeness.
research_questions: Which office items already carry reliable identifiers and can use native defaults?

already_counted.description: Missing identifier capture, physical handling, claim corrections, final checks, dispatch and filing exceptions remain.

incremental.description: Maintain routing and claim mappings and recover misclassified items.

approvals.approved_version: checked mail content and recipient snapshot from s4; changes void it
checked claim fields and payer snapshot from s4; changes void it

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central cuts 10 sorting, 19.5 claim entry and 5.6 filing give 35.1 gross and 33.6 net. Cautious case: poorly labelled mail leaves s1 unchanged, payer-specific forms leave s3 at 80%, and scanned records leave s7 at 90%; 7.4 gross less 1.5 upkeep gives 5.9, above low 5.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select report content with source-linked suggestions

steps.what: Read the source material and intended purpose before deciding report information
Compare source information with required report sections and mark candidate inclusions or exclusions

loop.purpose: Suggest source passages relevant to required report sections
loop.input: Identified passages, report purpose and section requirements
loop.output: Inclusion/exclusion suggestions with passage references and uncertainty
loop.check: Transcriptionist checks each suggestion for preserved meaning and clinically relevant omissions in s3
loop.stop: One suggestion set; ambiguous relevance stays undecided for human or clinician clarification
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text relevance depends on the purpose and clinical context, beyond fixed headings

steps.what: Decide which information should be included or excluded in reports and query clinical ambiguity
Apply the content decisions to the working reports without changing clinical meaning
Save the working reports as unsigned drafts for the existing clinical review workflow

tasks.design: Test required-section templates in the clinical transcription system in {OTHER} first, then add one bounded source-linked suggestion pass only for free-text relevance. The transcriptionist retains source reading, inclusion decisions and the edited unsigned draft; no clinical report is autonomously signed or transmitted.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comparing long source material to the report's intended sections is repetitive but contextual.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded language model can propose passage-to-section associations for human checking.
tasks.still_hard: Omitting a relevant negative finding or changing the significance of a statement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise clinically consequential ambiguity and ask the author instead of guessing.

ambition.what: No transfer of clinical judgement or signing rights is proposed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: source-linked language-model suggestions can assist free-text section comparison, but relevance and omission checks require human judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is content selection and edits to an existing unsigned report draft, not the whole transcription or subsequent clinical signature and transmission. These task estimates must not be added to overlapping whole-report estimates in a roll-up.

The clinical author supplies source transcript and report purpose; existing templates supply required sections. Transcriptionist reads and identifies the passages in s1. Missing purpose or source references stops suggestions and requires manual handling counted in s2/s3.

Native required sections are tested first. They cannot determine all free-text relevance; the loop removes initial sorting and cross-referencing only. All clinical content decisions and source reading remain.

Uncertain or misleading suggestions are manually redone in retained s2/s3 time, with incremental allowance for additional failures and template changes. The same-system working save is one fully retained share with no gate.
All shares are illustrative focal labour, unmeasured. Clinician clarification is existing unchanged outside labour; the helper introduces no extra clinical review requirement.
unknowns: Report purposes and local definition of what the transcriptionist may exclude.
research_questions: Do suggestions preserve relevant negative findings and cite the correct source passages?

already_counted.description: Source reading, suggestion correction, inclusion decisions and report edits remain.

incremental.description: Review template changes and recover failed suggestion passes beyond routine corrections.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central suggestion-stage cut 12 less upkeep 1 gives 11. Cautious case: uncommon report purposes and poorly segmented sources leave s2 at 90% retained, giving 3 gross and 2 net. Final decisions and source reading remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The transcriptionist spends less time copying data and producing first drafts while retaining identity, source and meaning checks.
reach: Medical records clerk: reconcile mapped fields to source records.
Billing clerk: validate claims from authorised service fields.
role.ambitious_version: Provide source-linked unsigned drafts and data packets for existing clinical review without expanding clinical authority.
